title: Broad E. coli complete-replicon progression for a Medium paper-deep Titans model
scientific_motivation: Test whether a substantially larger exact paper-deep MAC model can progress from weak local E. coli sequence learning toward useful genome- and genetic-parts-scale statistics when exposure is complete-replicon, ANI99-separated, and accession-balanced.

hypotheses.engineering: A 12-block d256 paper-exact model remains finite under stateful whole-replicon rotation, exact resume, FP32 functional memory, and qualified FP32 or BF16 attention.
hypotheses.learning: Complete-panel exposure improves broad held-out E. coli BPB over c16 across accessions rather than one chromosome.
hypotheses.generation: Scaling reduces six-mer, GC, coding-density, gene-length, and intergenic calibration error without decoder-induced diversity collapse.
hypotheses.memory: At least ten of twelve memory blocks retain immediate and delayed controlled association while long-stream states remain finite.

scope_limitations: Training is E. coli only; other Escherichia species are evaluation-only outgroups.
E25 and E100 are adaptive-only exploratory scale gates and cannot establish adaptive-memory benefit.
E100 is a documented warm-start continuation on E100-minus-E25 accessions, not an independent-from-scratch run.
Generated ORFs, gene calls, codon patterns, or upstream motifs are statistical diagnostics and not evidence of biological function, expression, viability, or safety.

claim_language.supported_after_e25: the Medium adaptive model is stable and improves broad held-out E. coli modeling sufficiently to justify E100
claim_language.supported_after_e100: the adaptive model is useful as an exploratory E. coli sequence model and merits matched controls
claim_language.not_supported: adaptive-memory superiority, functional genes, promoter activity, whole-chromosome generation, or broad bacterial generalization

dataset.source_data_fingerprint: inherited Stage C ordered-stream dataset hash required at run time
dataset.subset_manifest_fingerprint: frozen E25, E100-additions, validation, and test panel hashes required at run time
dataset.eligibility: train-split E. coli complete genomes only; CheckM completeness >=95 and contamination <=2; one representative per ANI99 group before repeats
dataset.continuity: each chromosome or plasmid is an independent ordered stream; replicons are never concatenated
dataset.balance: deterministic maximin ANI order with available phylogroup and GC-bin balancing
dataset.isolation: complete ANI99 groups remain exclusive to train, validation, or test

tokenizer.name: nonoverlap_6mer_v1
tokenizer.normalization: unchanged from the frozen Stage C ordered-stream dataset

decision_gates.data: Every panel hash verifies; only complete high-quality E. coli assemblies are selected; panels are nested; held-out ANI99 groups do not overlap training.
decision_gates.qualification: Exact resume passes; every tested tensor is finite; memory state is FP32; choose the highest-throughput FP32/BF16-attention batch using <=70% A100 memory and <=0.005 BPB parity error.
decision_gates.e25_prediction: Median held-out accession BPB <=1.96, at least 0.02 below the broad-panel c16 baseline, paired-accession bootstrap upper 95% bound below zero, and at least 75% of accessions improve.
decision_gates.e25_memory: Immediate and delayed controlled association are positive in at least ten of twelve blocks with zero paper-exact conditioning interventions.
decision_gates.e25_generation: Aligned six-mer diversity remains within 0.95-1.05 of reference; six-mer JSD improves >=10%, GC error falls, and at least three predefined genome/parts metric families improve over c16.
decision_gates.e100: Median held-out BPB <=1.92; at least ten of twelve accessions improve over E25; diversity does not collapse; at least four predefined genome/parts metric families improve.
decision_gates.stop: Do not alter thresholds after observing results. Failed gates remain visible and stop the next training allocation.

primary_exploratory: held-out BPB by accession and ANI99 group
paired accession bootstrap versus c16 and E25
memory: retrieval, update, drift, gate and gradient trajectories
immediate and delayed controlled association by block
genome_and_parts: GC and k-mer JSD through k=6
coding density, gene and intergenic lengths
codon usage, stop-codon frequency and frame periodicity
representations: embedding and memory projections with GC and coordinate controls
held-out outgroup and anomaly scoring at fixed false-positive rate

prohibited_inferences: No adaptive-memory benefit claim without a matched no-memory E100 comparison.
No functional gene, promoter, operon, viability, fitness, pathogenicity, or safety claim from generation.
No taxonomic representation claim from PCA alone.
No broad Escherichia or bacterial claim from E. coli-only fitting.
